newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico bolsa turns to underperformers, dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico bolsa turns to underperformers, dull trade.

text.p: Infrequently traded and cheap stocks rallied on what was otherwise a dull day for the Mexican stock market.
The winners list at the close of trade was headed by publishers Grupo Fernandez, followed by steelmakers Sidek, whose series B shares gained 12.84 percent and 10.76 percent, respectively.

"Volume was thin and the only remarkable feature was that infrequently traded stocks were in most demand and chalked up heavy gains," said Leonor Gonzalez, technical analyst at the BBV-Probursa brokerage.
Brokers said investors often turn to stocks whose prices have lagged behind, but whose fundamentals are good, when the blue chips are moving sideways.

Some traders said they bought Fernandez ahead of what they expected to be a good third quarter report. Others said they bought Sidek after it had been revalued in the U.S. Grupo Mexico was in third place among the leaders, due to short covering by some investors, traders added. The leading IPC index closed 15.97 points up, 0.48 percent, at 3,318.95. Volume was a dull 66.6 million shares. Winners outnumbered losers by 44 to 25, out of 94 stocks traded.
Gonzalez said that stock prices were also held up by technical signs.
"The market is in the middle of a wide band, between 3,320 and 3,350 points. We are still in a short-term upward channel, which could take us to new all-time highs, if we stay there," she said.

Thin volume showed, however, that many traders were cautious with a long weekend ahead and awaited the publication of U.S. inflation on Friday. Mexican markets will be closed on Monday, September 16 for the Independence Day holiday.
